summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundle unrelated to CLI purpose
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/... into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then execFileSync's it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle (shuffled string-array decoder WV8StW over hex table n7gIxM, hex-mangled identifiers, "// @bun @bun-cjs" header) that is not derivable from the package's advertised purpose (a OneReach 'orest' publishing CLI). setup.mjs itself is also obfuscated despite being described as a simple downloader. The Bun runtime is not needed for a Node CLI, and the executed bundle's cover-story name ('math_init') does not correspond to any documented functionality. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the runtime fetch is from an official source, but that runtime is then used at install time to execute an opaque obfuscated payload shipped inside the package, evading scanners that inspect only Node-resolved code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
